name: Asian elephant
distinguishingTraits: Smaller, more rounded ears than an African elephant
A domed head with two prominent bumps
A long, muscular trunk used for breathing, smelling, touching and grasping
typicalBehaviour: Uses its trunk to gather grass, leaves and other food
Bathes or sprays water and dust to cool and protect its skin
Lives in social family groups led by experienced females
safeVisitorFacts: The Singapore Zoo herd at Elephants of Asia is all female.
Mud and dust help protect elephant skin from sun and insects.
Watch quietly from the visitor area and follow keeper instructions during feeding sessions.

name: Malayan tiger
distinguishingTraits: Orange coat with bold black stripes and white areas around the face and underside
A long striped tail used for balance
A muscular body with a stripe pattern unique to each individual
typicalBehaviour: Usually solitary outside of mothers caring for cubs
May patrol, scent-mark, rest in shade or enter water
Is most active around cooler parts of the day
safeVisitorFacts: A tiger's stripe pattern is unique, like a fingerprint.
Malayan tigers are native to Peninsular Malaysia.
Remain behind visitor barriers and never imitate prey sounds or attempt to attract an animal.

name: Orangutan
distinguishingTraits: Very long arms adapted for moving through trees
typicalBehaviour: Climbs, swings and moves carefully through the canopy
Forages for fruit, leaves and other plant foods
safeVisitorFacts: The name orangutan comes from Malay words meaning person of the forest.
Orangutans spend much of their time above the ground.
Keep food secured and never feed wildlife unless a supervised programme explicitly allows it.

name: African penguin
distinguishingTraits: Black back and white belly with a black chest band
Pink skin patches above the eyes
A compact body with flipper-like wings
typicalBehaviour: Swims using its flippers for propulsion
Rests, preens and socialises in groups on land
Uses calls to recognise its partner and chicks
safeVisitorFacts: African penguins live on the coasts of southern Africa, not in Antarctica.
Their pink eye patches help release body heat.
Do not tap viewing glass or use flash where signs prohibit it.

name: Giraffe
distinguishingTraits: An extremely long neck and long legs
A tan coat covered in irregular brown patches
Two horn-like ossicones on top of the head
typicalBehaviour: Browses leaves high in trees using a long tongue
Walks slowly across open habitat and may gather in loose groups
safeVisitorFacts: A giraffe's patch pattern is unique to the individual.
Its long, dark tongue helps grasp leaves.
Use only food supplied during an authorised feeding session and follow keeper instructions.
